claim: Drosophila dorsal air sac development depends on Decapentaplegic (Dpp) and Fibroblast growth factor (FGF) proteins produced by the wing imaginal disc.
source: Drosophila dorsal air sac development depends on Decapentaplegic (Dpp) and Fibroblast growth factor (FGF) proteins produced by the wing imaginal disc and transported by cytonemes to the air sac primordium (ASP).
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract and supported by references to previous work (Roy et al., 2011; Sato and Kornberg, 2002).

claim: Dpp and FGF proteins are transported by cytonemes to the air sac primordium (ASP).
source: Drosophila dorsal air sac development depends on Decapentaplegic (Dpp) and Fibroblast growth factor (FGF) proteins produced by the wing imaginal disc and transported by cytonemes to the air sac primordium (ASP).
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract and supported by references to previous work (Roy et al., 2014).

claim: Dpp and FGF signaling in the ASP was dependent on components of the planar cell polarity (PCP) system in the disc.
source: Dpp and FGF signaling in the ASP was dependent on components of the planar cell polarity (PCP) system in the disc, and neither Dpp- nor FGF-receiving cytonemes extended over mutant disc cells that lacked them.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data shown in Figures 3, 4, and 6.

claim: Neither Dpp- nor FGF-receiving cytonemes extended over mutant disc cells that lacked PCP components.
source: Dpp and FGF signaling in the ASP was dependent on components of the planar cell polarity (PCP) system in the disc, and neither Dpp- nor FGF-receiving cytonemes extended over mutant disc cells that lacked them.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and demonstrated by clonal analysis shown in Figure 3.

claim: ASP cytonemes normally navigate through extracellular matrix (ECM) composed of collagen, laminin, Dally and Dally-like (Dlp) proteins.
source: ASP cytonemes normally navigate through extracellular matrix (ECM) composed of collagen, laminin, Dally and Dally-like (Dlp) proteins that are stratified in layers over the disc cells.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by imaging data in Figure 7.

claim: ECM proteins (collagen, laminin, Dally, and Dlp) are stratified in layers over the disc cells.
source: ASP cytonemes normally navigate through extracellular matrix (ECM) composed of collagen, laminin, Dally and Dally-like (Dlp) proteins that are stratified in layers over the disc cells.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and demonstrated by confocal imaging in Figure 7D-F.

claim: ECM over PCP mutant cells had reduced levels of laminin, Dally and Dlp.
source: However, ECM over PCP mutant cells had reduced levels of laminin, Dally and Dlp, and whereas Dpp-receiving ASP cytonemes navigated in the Dally layer and required Dally (but not Dlp), FGF-receiving ASP cytonemes navigated in the Dlp layer, requiring Dlp (but not Dally).
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and demonstrated by immunofluorescence data in Figure 5.

claim: Dpp-receiving ASP cytonemes navigated in the Dally layer and required Dally (but not Dlp).
source: However, ECM over PCP mutant cells had reduced levels of laminin, Dally and Dlp, and whereas Dpp-receiving ASP cytonemes navigated in the Dally layer and required Dally (but not Dlp), FGF-receiving ASP cytonemes navigated in the Dlp layer, requiring Dlp (but not Dally).
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figures 6 and 7 showing differential requirements and spatial segregation.

claim: FGF-receiving ASP cytonemes navigated in the Dlp layer, requiring Dlp (but not Dally).
source: However, ECM over PCP mutant cells had reduced levels of laminin, Dally and Dlp, and whereas Dpp-receiving ASP cytonemes navigated in the Dally layer and required Dally (but not Dlp), FGF-receiving ASP cytonemes navigated in the Dlp layer, requiring Dlp (but not Dally).
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figures 6 and 7 showing differential requirements and spatial segregation.

claim: Cytonemes interact directly and specifically with proteins in the stratified ECM.
source: These findings suggest that cytonemes interact directly and specifically with proteins in the stratified ECM.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the findings in the abstract, based on the differential requirements and spatial segregation observed.

claim: Signaling proteins that regulate development are transported along actin-based filopodia (cytonemes).
source: Studies of Drosophila, chick, zebrafish, and cultured human cells show that the signaling proteins that regulate development are transported along actin-based filopodia (cytonemes) and exchange at synapses where the cells that produce them contact the cells that receive and respond to them (Roy et al., 2014 and reviewed in Kornberg and Roy, 2014; Pröls et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by multiple citations to previous work.

claim: Signaling proteins exchange at synapses where producing cells contact receiving cells.
source: Studies of Drosophila, chick, zebrafish, and cultured human cells show that the signaling proteins that regulate development are transported along actin-based filopodia (cytonemes) and exchange at synapses where the cells that produce them contact the cells that receive and respond to them (Roy et al., 2014 and reviewed in Kornberg and Roy, 2014; Pröls et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations to previous work.

claim: The distance between source and receiving cells can be as much as 100 µm in the wing disc.
source: The large distances between the source and receiving cells in some of these contexts (as much as 100 µm in the wing disc and 150 µm in the chick limb bud) highlights the question that this work investigates - how cytonemes extend to reach their targets.
evidence: This is stated directly in the introduction as a factual observation.

claim: The distance between source and receiving cells can be as much as 150 µm in the chick limb bud.
source: The large distances between the source and receiving cells in some of these contexts (as much as 100 µm in the wing disc and 150 µm in the chick limb bud) highlights the question that this work investigates - how cytonemes extend to reach their targets.
evidence: This is stated directly in the introduction as a factual observation.

claim: The ASP is a tracheal tube that develops in the third instar larva under the influence of Dpp and FGF produced in the wing disc.
source: The cytonemes we characterized were made by the ASP, a tracheal tube that develops in the third instar larva under the influence of Dpp and FGF that are produced in the wing disc (Roy et al., 2011; Sato and Kornberg, 2002).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Cytonemes that mediate the exchange of Dpp and FGF contain the Dpp receptor Thickveins (Tkv) or the FGF receptor Breathless (Btl).
source: The cytonemes that mediate the exchange of these proteins contain the Dpp receptor Thickveins (Tkv) or the FGF receptor Breathless (Btl), extending from the basal surface of the ASP cells and synapsing with Dpp- or FGF-producing disc cells, respectively (Roy et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citation to previous work.

claim: ASP cytonemes extend from the basal surface of the ASP cells and synapse with Dpp- or FGF-producing disc cells.
source: The cytonemes that mediate the exchange of these proteins contain the Dpp receptor Thickveins (Tkv) or the FGF receptor Breathless (Btl), extending from the basal surface of the ASP cells and synapsing with Dpp- or FGF-producing disc cells, respectively (Roy et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citation to previous work.

claim: The ASP lies underneath the basement membrane that envelops the wing disc.
source: The ASP lies underneath the basement membrane that envelops the wing disc (Guha et al., 2009), and although the space they traverse has not been analyzed, it presumably has characteristics of prototypical extracellular matrix (ECM, reviewed in Broadie et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citation to previous work.

claim: The space that ASP cytonemes traverse presumably has characteristics of prototypical extracellular matrix (ECM).
source: The ASP lies underneath the basement membrane that envelops the wing disc (Guha et al., 2009), and although the space they traverse has not been analyzed, it presumably has characteristics of prototypical extracellular matrix (ECM, reviewed in Broadie et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated as a presumption in the introduction based on general knowledge of ECM.

claim: The number and distribution of ASP cytonemes depend on the production of Dpp and FGF in the disc.
source: The number and distribution of ASP cytonemes depend on the production of Dpp and FGF in the disc and on their respective receptors in the ASP, but it is not known whether the cells between the producing and receiving cells (henceforth called 'intermediate cells') also contribute to cytoneme-mediated signaling.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as established knowledge from previous work.

claim: The number and distribution of ASP cytonemes depend on their respective receptors in the ASP.
source: The number and distribution of ASP cytonemes depend on the production of Dpp and FGF in the disc and on their respective receptors in the ASP, but it is not known whether the cells between the producing and receiving cells (henceforth called 'intermediate cells') also contribute to cytoneme-mediated signaling.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as established knowledge from previous work.

claim: PCP is an aspect of cell polarity that establishes a singular, shared bipolar orientation across an epithelial sheet.
source: PCP is an aspect of cell polarity that establishes a singular, shared bipolar orientation across an epithelial sheet (reviewed in Goodrich and Strutt, 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citation to a review.

claim: In the insect cuticle, PCP is responsible for the coordinated and consistent orientation of hairs and bristles.
source: In the insect cuticle, it is responsible for the coordinated and consistent orientation of hairs and bristles.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as established knowledge about PCP function.

claim: PCP is manifested in the asymmetric subcellular localization of proteins such as Frizzled (Fz), Dishevelled (Dsh), Diego (Dgo), Van Gogh (Vang), and Prickle (Pk).
source: PCP is also manifested in the asymmetric subcellular localization of proteins such as Frizzled (Fz, a seven-pass transmembrane protein), Dishevelled (Dsh) and Diego (Dgo, cytosolic proteins) to one side and Van Gogh (Vang, a four-pass transmembrane protein) and Prickle (Pk, a cytosolic protein) to the other.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as established knowledge about PCP.

claim: Fz, Dsh, Dgo, Vang and Pk are constituents of the core PCP pathway in Drosophila.
source: Fz, Dsh, Dgo, Vang and Pk are constituents of the core PCP pathway in Drosophila, and all are required for planar orientation and polarization.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as established knowledge about PCP.

claim: All core PCP components are required for planar orientation and polarization.
source: Fz, Dsh, Dgo, Vang and Pk are constituents of the core PCP pathway in Drosophila, and all are required for planar orientation and polarization.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as established knowledge about PCP.

claim: Absent any one core PCP component, hairs and bristles lack normal polarity.
source: Absent any one and the hairs and bristles lack normal polarity.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as established knowledge about PCP mutant phenotypes.

claim: In Drosophila genetic mosaics, cells to one side of PCP mutant cells have abnormal planar polarity.
source: In Drosophila genetic mosaics, cells to one side of PCP mutant cells also have abnormal planar polarity (Casal et al., 2002; Taylor et al., 1998; Vinson and Adler, 1987), leading to the idea that PCP involves a system of cell-cell interactions that coordinate the polarity of neighboring cells and propagate orientation long-range.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations to previous work.

claim: PCP involves a system of cell-cell interactions that coordinate the polarity of neighboring cells and propagate orientation long-range.
source: In Drosophila genetic mosaics, cells to one side of PCP mutant cells also have abnormal planar polarity (Casal et al., 2002; Taylor et al., 1998; Vinson and Adler, 1987), leading to the idea that PCP involves a system of cell-cell interactions that coordinate the polarity of neighboring cells and propagate orientation long-range.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as an interpretation based on cited observations.

claim: Studies of cells deficient for components of the PCP system in Drosophila report loss of several features of normal apical-basal polarity.
source: Studies of cells deficient for components of the PCP system in Drosophila (Djiane et al., 2005; Harumoto et al., 2010) and mouse (Tao et al., 2009; Vandenberg and Sassoon, 2009) report loss of several features of normal apical-basal polarity.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Studies of cells deficient for components of the PCP system in mouse report loss of several features of normal apical-basal polarity.
source: Studies of cells deficient for components of the PCP system in Drosophila (Djiane et al., 2005; Harumoto et al., 2010) and mouse (Tao et al., 2009; Vandenberg and Sassoon, 2009) report loss of several features of normal apical-basal polarity.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations to previous work.

claim: PCP components have been implicated in the deposition and remodeling of the ECM.
source: PCP components have been implicated in the deposition and remodeling of the ECM (Dohn et al., 2013; Goto et al., 2005; Williams et al., 2012a, 2012b), axon guidance (Fenstermaker et al., 2010; Mrkusich et al., 2011; Shafer et al., 2011; Gombos et al., 2015 and reviewed in Yam and Charron, 2013) and cell migration (Carreira-Barbosa et al., 2003; Dohn et al., 2013; Roszko et al., 2015; Tatin et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations to previous work.

claim: PCP components have been implicated in axon guidance.
source: PCP components have been implicated in the deposition and remodeling of the ECM (Dohn et al., 2013; Goto et al., 2005; Williams et al., 2012a, 2012b), axon guidance (Fenstermaker et al., 2010; Mrkusich et al., 2011; Shafer et al., 2011; Gombos et al., 2015 and reviewed in Yam and Charron, 2013) and cell migration (Carreira-Barbosa et al., 2003; Dohn et al., 2013; Roszko et al., 2015; Tatin et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations to previous work.

claim: PCP components have been implicated in cell migration.
source: PCP components have been implicated in the deposition and remodeling of the ECM (Dohn et al., 2013; Goto et al., 2005; Williams et al., 2012a, 2012b), axon guidance (Fenstermaker et al., 2010; Mrkusich et al., 2011; Shafer et al., 2011; Gombos et al., 2015 and reviewed in Yam and Charron, 2013) and cell migration (Carreira-Barbosa et al., 2003; Dohn et al., 2013; Roszko et al., 2015; Tatin et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations to previous work.

claim: The glypicans Dally and Dally-like (Dlp) are components of the ECM that contribute essential functions to signaling.
source: The glypicans Dally and Dally-like (Dlp) are components of the ECM that contribute essential functions to signaling (Han et al., 2004; Fujise et al., 2003; Han et al., 2005; Lin and Perrimon, 1999; Yan and Lin, 2007; Yan et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Dally and Dlp are glycophosphatidylinositol (GPI)-anchored and are modified with heparan sulfate glycosaminoglycan (GAG) chains.
source: They are glycophosphatidylinositol (GPI)-anchored and are modified with heparan sulfate glycosaminoglycan (GAG) chains.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as established knowledge about Dally and Dlp structure.

claim: It is assumed that both Dally and Dlp function externally.
source: Although an intracellular function has been reported for Dlp in Hh-producing cells (Callejo et al., 2011), it is assumed that both Dally and Dlp function externally.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a general assumption, with one exception noted.

claim: An intracellular function has been reported for Dlp in Hh-producing cells.
source: Although an intracellular function has been reported for Dlp in Hh-producing cells (Callejo et al., 2011), it is assumed that both Dally and Dlp function externally.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Cytonemes do not pass over patches of cells that are deficient for GAG-modified HSPGs.
source: Alternatively, the recent report that cytonemes do not pass over patches of cells that are deficient for GAG-modified HSPGs suggests that impairment of cytoneme-mediated transport may account for the mutant phenotypes (Bischoff et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Integrin function is required for axonal pathfinding.
source: Integrin function is required for axonal pathfinding, TGF-β signaling and for interactions of migrating cells and cell protrusions with the ECM (Dominguez-Giménez et al., 2007; Han et al., 2012; Myers et al., 2011; Robles and Gomez, 2006; Vuoriluoto et al., 2008 and reviewed in Munger and Sheppard, 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Integrin function is required for TGF-β signaling.
source: Integrin function is required for axonal pathfinding, TGF-β signaling and for interactions of migrating cells and cell protrusions with the ECM (Dominguez-Giménez et al., 2007; Han et al., 2012; Myers et al., 2011; Robles and Gomez, 2006; Vuoriluoto et al., 2008 and reviewed in Munger and Sheppard, 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Integrin function is required for interactions of migrating cells and cell protrusions with the ECM.
source: Integrin function is required for axonal pathfinding, TGF-β signaling and for interactions of migrating cells and cell protrusions with the ECM (Dominguez-Giménez et al., 2007; Han et al., 2012; Myers et al., 2011; Robles and Gomez, 2006; Vuoriluoto et al., 2008 and reviewed in Munger and Sheppard, 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations to previous work.

claim: ASP morphology was abnormal in pk and Vang mutants.
source: In pk and Vang (Figure 1D–F), dachsous (ds) and fat (ft) mutants (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A–C), and in larvae that express misshapen, dRhoA, drok, dRac1, multiple wing hair, or Leukocyte-antigen-related-like RNAi (Table 1), ASP morphology was abnormal.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by images in Figure 1D-F.

claim: ASP morphology was abnormal in dachsous (ds) and fat (ft) mutants.
source: In pk and Vang (Figure 1D–F), dachsous (ds) and fat (ft) mutants (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A–C), and in larvae that express misshapen, dRhoA, drok, dRac1, multiple wing hair, or Leukocyte-antigen-related-like RNAi (Table 1), ASP morphology was abnormal.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by images in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A-C.

claim: ASP morphology was abnormal in larvae that express misshapen, dRhoA, drok, dRac1, multiple wing hair, or Leukocyte-antigen-related-like RNAi.
source: In pk and Vang (Figure 1D–F), dachsous (ds) and fat (ft) mutants (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A–C), and in larvae that express misshapen, dRhoA, drok, dRac1, multiple wing hair, or Leukocyte-antigen-related-like RNAi (Table 1), ASP morphology was abnormal.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Table 1.

claim: All mutant ASPs with pk and Vang genotypes were abnormal.
source: Although the abnormalities of the pk and Vang mutant ASPs shown in Figure 1E and F are among the most extreme that were observed, all mutant ASPs with these genotypes were abnormal.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a summary of observations.

claim: In pk and Vang mutants, growth was stunted.
source: In pk and Vang mutants, growth was stunted, the morphology of every ASP was abnormal (approximately 10% were duplicated), and the ASP cytonemes were less abundant and shorter than normal (Figure 1E,F and Table 2).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by images in Figure 1E,F.

claim: In pk and Vang mutants, approximately 10% of ASPs were duplicated.
source: In pk and Vang mutants, growth was stunted, the morphology of every ASP was abnormal (approximately 10% were duplicated), and the ASP cytonemes were less abundant and shorter than normal (Figure 1E,F and Table 2).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a quantitative observation.

claim: In pk and Vang mutants, ASP cytonemes were less abundant and shorter than normal.
source: In pk and Vang mutants, growth was stunted, the morphology of every ASP was abnormal (approximately 10% were duplicated), and the ASP cytonemes were less abundant and shorter than normal (Figure 1E,F and Table 2).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by images in Figure 1E,F and quantitative data in Table 2.

claim: Expression of pkRNAi and VangRNAi constructs in tracheal cells did not affect either ASP morphology or ASP cytonemes.
source: Expression of the RNAi constructs in tracheal cells did not affect either ASP morphology or ASP cytonemes (Figure 2A,B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by images in Figure 2A,B.

claim: ASP morphology was abnormal and cytonemes were reduced in number and length when pkRNAi or VangRNAi were expressed in the dorsal region of the wing disc.
source: In contrast, ASP morphology was abnormal and cytonemes were reduced in number and length when pkRNAi or VangRNAi were expressed in the dorsal region of the wing disc where the ASP is located (Figure 2F,G).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by images in Figure 2F,G.

claim: Loss- and gain-of-function conditions for pk and other PCP genes have similar effects on planar polarity.
source: Similar results were obtained by ectopic over-expression of pk and Vang in the dorsal wing disc (Figure 2—figure supplement 1), consistent with previous studies showing that loss- and gain-of-function conditions for pk and other PCP genes have similar effects on planar polarity (Adler et al., 2000; Casal et al., 2002; Taylor et al., 1998; Tree et al., 2002; Vinson and Adler, 1987).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Over expression of either fz or fmi had no apparent effect on ASP morphology or development.
source: Over expression of either fz or fmi had no apparent effect on ASP morphology or development (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Grunge (Gug) is required specifically in disc cells for ASP development.
source: Expression of RNAi constructs directed against other genes of the PCP system (Table 1) identified Grunge (Gug) to be another candidate function that is required specifically in disc cells (Figure 2C,H).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by images in Figure 2C,H and data in Table 1.

claim: Gug encodes the Drosophila homolog of the Atrophin co-repressor.
source: Gug encodes the Drosophila homolog of the Atrophin co-repressor (Erkner et al., 2002; Zhang et al., 2002) and has been proposed to function in the Fat/Dachsous arm of the PCP system (Fanto et al., 2003).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Gug has been proposed to function in the Fat/Dachsous arm of the PCP system.
source: Gug encodes the Drosophila homolog of the Atrophin co-repressor (Erkner et al., 2002; Zhang et al., 2002) and has been proposed to function in the Fat/Dachsous arm of the PCP system (Fanto et al., 2003).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by citation to previous work.

claim: RNAi directed against dRhoA, mwh, and Lar resulted in abnormal ASP phenotypes after expression in either the ASP or disc.
source: RNAi directed against several other genes that are required for PCP function (e.g., dRhoA, mwh, Lar) resulted in abnormal ASP phenotypes after expression in either the ASP or disc (Table 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Table 1.

claim: Ten pk and nine Vang clones were identified near the lateral side of the ASP or near the ASP tip.
source: Ten pk and nine Vang clones were identified near the lateral side of the ASP or near the ASP tip; none of the clonal areas were traversed by cytonemes.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a quantitative observation from clonal analysis.

claim: None of the pk or Vang clonal areas were traversed by cytonemes.
source: Ten pk and nine Vang clones were identified near the lateral side of the ASP or near the ASP tip; none of the clonal areas were traversed by cytonemes.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by images in Figure 3.

claim: Cytonemes were present at the periphery of pk and Vang mutant clones, but no cytonemes were found inside mutant territory.
source: Cytonemes were present at the periphery of mutant clones, but no cytonemes were found inside mutant territory.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by images in Figure 3.

claim: Pk and Vang are essential in 'intermediate' disc cells in order for cytonemes to extend over their surface.
source: These results suggest that Pk and Vang are essential in 'intermediate' disc cells in order for cytonemes to extend over their surface.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an interpretation of the clonal analysis data.

claim: Cytonemes that extend from the ASP to the wing disc are essential for Dpp and FGF signaling in the ASP.
source: Our previous studies showed that cytonemes that extend from the ASP to the wing disc are essential for Dpp and FGF signaling in the ASP (Roy et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Under normal conditions, cells in the medial region of the ASP activate Dpp signal transduction.
source: Under normal conditions, cells in the medial region of the ASP activate Dpp signal transduction (Figure 4A and Roy et al., 2014) and cells at the tip activate FGF signal transduction (Figure 4D and Roy et al., 2014; Sato and Kornberg, 2002).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by images in Figure 4A and citations to previous work.

claim: Under normal conditions, cells at the tip of the ASP activate FGF signal transduction.
source: Under normal conditions, cells in the medial region of the ASP activate Dpp signal transduction (Figure 4A and Roy et al., 2014) and cells at the tip activate FGF signal transduction (Figure 4D and Roy et al., 2014; Sato and Kornberg, 2002).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by images in Figure 4D and citations to previous work.

claim: In pk and Vang mutants, Dpp and FGF signal transduction in the ASP were reduced.
source: In pk and Vang mutants, Dpp and FGF signal transduction in the ASP were reduced (Figure 4B,C,E,F), confirming the importance of these functions for signaling in the ASP.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by images in Figure 4B,C,E,F.

claim: Cells in pk and Vang mutant ASPs appeared to be larger and reduced in number compared to controls.
source: Cells in mutant ASPs appeared to be larger and reduced in number compared to controls, and their morphology appeared to be abnormal.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an observation from imaging data.

claim: The wing disc is enveloped by a collagen-containing ECM.
source: The wing disc is enveloped by a collagen-containing ECM, and because the ASP is situated between the basal surface of the disc and ECM (Guha et al., 2009), the ASP cytonemes do not normally penetrate from outside the ECM to reach the disc.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by citation to previous work.

claim: The ASP is situated between the basal surface of the disc and ECM.
source: The wing disc is enveloped by a collagen-containing ECM, and because the ASP is situated between the basal surface of the disc and ECM (Guha et al., 2009), the ASP cytonemes do not normally penetrate from outside the ECM to reach the disc.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by citation to previous work.

claim: ASP cytonemes do not normally penetrate from outside the ECM to reach the disc.
source: The wing disc is enveloped by a collagen-containing ECM, and because the ASP is situated between the basal surface of the disc and ECM (Guha et al., 2009), the ASP cytonemes do not normally penetrate from outside the ECM to reach the disc.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an inference based on the anatomical arrangement.

claim: ASP cytonemes navigate along, or at some distance from the basal surface of the disc cells.
source: Rather, they navigate along, or at some distance from the basal surface of the disc cells, and they presumably encounter the ECM in a manner that has not been defined.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an interpretation of the anatomical arrangement.

claim: The structure of the ECM is sensitive to both increased and reduced Mmp2 expression.
source: We previously observed that the structure of the ECM is sensitive to both increased and reduced Mmp2 expression, and that dis-regulation of Mmp2 reduces ASP growth and signaling and perturbs morphogenesis (Guha et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Dis-regulation of Mmp2 reduces ASP growth and signaling and perturbs morphogenesis.
source: We previously observed that the structure of the ECM is sensitive to both increased and reduced Mmp2 expression, and that dis-regulation of Mmp2 reduces ASP growth and signaling and perturbs morphogenesis (Guha et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Expression of dallyRNAi or dlpRNAi in the disc perturbed ASP morphology and reduced the number of ASP cytonemes.
source: Expression of dallyRNAi or dlpRNAi in the disc perturbed ASP morphology and reduced the number of ASP cytonemes (Figure 2I,J), an indication that the Dally and Dlp HSPGs are essential ECM components for ASP morphogenesis and signaling.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by images in Figure 2I,J.

claim: Dally and Dlp HSPGs are essential ECM components for ASP morphogenesis and signaling.
source: Expression of dallyRNAi or dlpRNAi in the disc perturbed ASP morphology and reduced the number of ASP cytonemes (Figure 2I,J), an indication that the Dally and Dlp HSPGs are essential ECM components for ASP morphogenesis and signaling.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an interpretation of the RNAi data.

claim: Expression of dallyRNAi or dlpRNAi had no effect when expressed in the ASP.
source: Expression of these RNAi constructs had no effect when expressed in the ASP (Figure 2D,E).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by images in Figure 2D,E.

claim: The level of Dlp was reduced approximately 60% in the areas over pk and Vang mutant clones.
source: Using antibody directed against Dlp, we found that the level of Dlp was reduced approximately 60% in the areas over pk and Vang mutant clones (Figure 5A–D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by images in Figure 5A-D.

claim: Dally fluorescence was reduced approximately 45% in the engrailed expression domain in discs in which either pkRNAi or VangRNAi was expressed in the posterior compartment.
source: As indicated by YFP fluorescence, Dally was present at similar levels over the wing disc, but fluorescence was reduced approximately 45% in the engrailed expression domain in discs in which either pkRNAi or VangRNAi was expressed in the posterior compartment under the control of engrailed-Gal4 (Figure 5E–G).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by images in Figure 5E-G.

claim: pk loss-of-function clones had reduced levels of laminin.
source: pk loss-of-function clones also had reduced levels of laminin (Figure 5H,I).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by images in Figure 5H,I.

claim: pk and Vang are necessary to maintain normal levels of Dally, Dlp and laminin in the ECM.
source: Together, these observations indicate that pk and Vang are necessary to maintain normal levels of Dally, Dlp and laminin in the ECM.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an interpretation of the data on ECM protein levels.

claim: No changes in amounts of either Dally or Dlp RNA were detected when normal discs were compared to pk or Vang mutant discs.
source: We did not detect changes in amounts of either Dally or Dlp RNA when normal discs were compared to pk or Vang mutant discs (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by qRT-PCR data in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Cells in mutant Vang clones appeared to retain normal distributions of Dlg.
source: Whereas cells in mutant Vang clones appeared to retain normal distributions of Dlg, which is consistent with the normal morphological appearance of the columnar disc cells, levels of aPKC were elevated and extended more basally than normal.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by images in Figure 5—figure supplement 2.

claim: Levels of aPKC were elevated and extended more basally than normal in mutant Vang clones.
source: Whereas cells in mutant Vang clones appeared to retain normal distributions of Dlg, which is consistent with the normal morphological appearance of the columnar disc cells, levels of aPKC were elevated and extended more basally than normal.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by images in Figure 5—figure supplement 2.

claim: The PCP system downregulates aPKC.
source: The apparent downregulation of aPKC by the PCP system, which has been reported previously in studies of the Drosophila eye (Djiane et al., 2005) and wing (Harumoto et al., 2010), indicates that some aspects of the apical/basal polarity are PCP-dependent.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by citations to previous work and current data.

claim: Some aspects of the apical/basal polarity are PCP-dependent.
source: The apparent downregulation of aPKC by the PCP system, which has been reported previously in studies of the Drosophila eye (Djiane et al., 2005) and wing (Harumoto et al., 2010), indicates that some aspects of the apical/basal polarity are PCP-dependent.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an interpretation of the aPKC data.

claim: ASPs in dally80 and dlpA187 mutants were reduced in size and abnormally shaped.
source: Whereas expression of membrane-tethered mCherry (btl>CD8:Cherry) in the ASP of controls revealed a large bulbous organ with cytonemes extending from both the tip (arrow) and lateral (arrowhead) regions (Figure 6A), expression of mCherry in dally80 and dlpA187 mutants revealed ASPs that were reduced in size and abnormally shaped (Figure 6B,C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by images in Figure 6B,C.

claim: In the dally80 ASP, cytonemes extended primarily postero-laterally from the tip.
source: In the dally80 ASP, cytonemes extended primarily postero-laterally from the tip; in contrast, long cytonemes extended only along the dorsal/ventral axis from the lateral surface in the dlpA187 ASP.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by images in Figure 6B.

claim: In the dlpA187 ASP, long cytonemes extended only along the dorsal/ventral axis from the lateral surface.
source: In the dally80 ASP, cytonemes extended primarily postero-laterally from the tip; in contrast, long cytonemes extended only along the dorsal/ventral axis from the lateral surface in the dlpA187 ASP.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by images in Figure 6C.

claim: Loss of Dally reduced Dpp signaling, but it did not alter FGF signaling.
source: Loss of Dally reduced Dpp signaling, but it did not alter FGF signaling (Figure 6D,E,G,H).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by images in Figure 6D,E,G,H.

claim: Loss of Dlp reduced FGF signaling but not Dpp signaling.
source: In contrast, loss of Dlp reduced FGF signaling but not Dpp signaling (Figure 6F,I).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by images in Figure 6F,I.

claim: The dorsal-oriented cytonemes that mediate Dpp signaling were primarily reduced in dally80 mutants.
source: This analysis confirms that whereas cytonemes extended postero-laterally from the ASP tip and along the dorsal/ventral axis from the medial ASP in approximately equal numbers under normal conditions, the dorsal-oriented cytonemes that mediate Dpp signaling were primarily reduced in dally80 mutants and the postero-laterally oriented cytonemes were primarily reduced in dlpA187 mutants.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Rose plots in Figure 6J.

claim: The postero-laterally oriented cytonemes were primarily reduced in dlpA187 mutants.
source: This analysis confirms that whereas cytonemes extended postero-laterally from the ASP tip and along the dorsal/ventral axis from the medial ASP in approximately equal numbers under normal conditions, the dorsal-oriented cytonemes that mediate Dpp signaling were primarily reduced in dally80 mutants and the postero-laterally oriented cytonemes were primarily reduced in dlpA187 mutants.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Rose plots in Figure 6J.

claim: The absence of lateral cytonemes in the dally loss-of-function condition correlates with the reduction of Dpp signaling.
source: Thus, the absence of lateral cytonemes in the dally loss-of-function condition and the absence of tip cytonemes in the dlp loss-of-function condition correlate with the reduction of Dpp and FGF signaling, respectively.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an interpretation of the correlation between cytoneme distribution and signaling.

claim: The absence of tip cytonemes in the dlp loss-of-function condition correlates with the reduction of FGF signaling.
source: Thus, the absence of lateral cytonemes in the dally loss-of-function condition and the absence of tip cytonemes in the dlp loss-of-function condition correlate with the reduction of Dpp and FGF signaling, respectively.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an interpretation of the correlation between cytoneme distribution and signaling.

claim: The presence of tip cytonemes in the dally loss-of-function condition correlates with FGF signaling in the ASP.
source: The presence of tip cytonemes in the dally loss-of-function condition correlates with FGF signaling in the ASP, and the presence of lateral cytonemes in dlp loss-of-function conditions correlates with Dpp signaling.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an interpretation of the correlation between cytoneme distribution and signaling.

claim: The presence of lateral cytonemes in dlp loss-of-function conditions correlates with Dpp signaling.
source: The presence of tip cytonemes in the dally loss-of-function condition correlates with FGF signaling in the ASP, and the presence of lateral cytonemes in dlp loss-of-function conditions correlates with Dpp signaling.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an interpretation of the correlation between cytoneme distribution and signaling.

claim: Cytonemes marked with Btl:Cherry extended over dally mutant clones and were apparently unchanged relative to controls.
source: Whereas cytonemes marked with Btl:Cherry extended over dally mutant clones and were apparently unchanged relative to controls, they did not extend over dlp mutant cells (Figure 6K,L).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by images in Figure 6K.

claim: Cytonemes marked with Btl:Cherry did not extend over dlp mutant cells.
source: Whereas cytonemes marked with Btl:Cherry extended over dally mutant clones and were apparently unchanged relative to controls, they did not extend over dlp mutant cells (Figure 6K,L).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by images in Figure 6L.

claim: Cytonemes marked with Tkv:Cherry extended over dlp mutant cells without apparent perturbation.
source: In contrast, cytonemes marked with Tkv:Cherry extended over dlp mutant cells without apparent perturbation, but they did not extend over dally mutant cells (Figure 6M,N).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by images in Figure 6N.

claim: Cytonemes marked with Tkv:Cherry did not extend over dally mutant cells.
source: In contrast, cytonemes marked with Tkv:Cherry extended over dlp mutant cells without apparent perturbation, but they did not extend over dally mutant cells (Figure 6M,N).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by images in Figure 6M.

claim: The Tkv- and Btl-containing cytonemes are separated in the space over the wing disc.
source: Simultaneous expression of Tkv:GFP and Btl:Cherry in the ASP marked the Tkv- and Btl-containing cytonemes, and sagittal projections of serial confocal sections (Figure 7A) and frontal sections (Figure 7B,C) of a specimen isolated from an early to mid L3 stage larva showed that these two types of cytonemes are separated in the space over the wing disc: the Tkv-containing cytonemes traverse a region further from the basal surface of the disc than the Btl-containing ones.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by images in Figure 7A-C.

claim: The Tkv-containing cytonemes traverse a region further from the basal surface of the disc than the Btl-containing ones.
source: Simultaneous expression of Tkv:GFP and Btl:Cherry in the ASP marked the Tkv- and Btl-containing cytonemes, and sagittal projections of serial confocal sections (Figure 7A) and frontal sections (Figure 7B,C) of a specimen isolated from an early to mid L3 stage larva showed that these two types of cytonemes are separated in the space over the wing disc: the Tkv-containing cytonemes traverse a region further from the basal surface of the disc than the Btl-containing ones.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by images in Figure 7A-C.

claim: Both the Tkv-containing and Btl-containing cytonemes extend from the tip at early to mid L3 stage.
source: Both the Tkv-containing and Btl-containing cytonemes extend from the tip at this stage (Roy et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Collagen, laminin, Dally, and Dlp were stratified above the basal surface of the disc epithelium.
source: Similar preparations imaged to identify Dally and Dlp (Figure 7D), and laminin, collagen and Dlp (Figure 7E), showed that these proteins were stratified above the basal surface of the disc epithelium.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by images in Figure 7D,E.

claim: Collagen was present in a discrete, distal-most layer.
source: Collagen was present in a discrete, distal-most layer.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by images in Figure 7E.

claim: Laminin was most prominent distally but it did not extend as far from the disc surface as collagen.
source: Laminin was also most prominent distally but it did not extend as far from the disc surface as collagen.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by images in Figure 7E.

claim: Dally was prominent distally, but Dally did not extend as far from the disc surface as collagen or laminin.
source: Dally was also prominent distally, but Dally did not extend as far from the disc surface as collagen or laminin.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by images in Figure 7D.

claim: Dlp was most prominent in the region more proximal to the basal surface of the disc epithelium.
source: Dlp was most prominent in the region more proximal to the basal surface of the disc epithelium.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by images in Figure 7D,E.

claim: The segregation of the Tkv-containing and Btl-containing cytoneme types to separate Dally and Dlp strata establishes the functional importance of ECM stratification.
source: The segregation of the Tkv-containing and Btl-containing cytoneme types to separate Dally and Dlp strata and the specific requirements for Dally and Dlp by Tkv-containing and Btl-containing cytonemes establishes the functional importance of ECM stratification.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an interpretation of the combined data on cytoneme segregation and HSPG requirements.

claim: ASP development was abnormal in the presence of mysRNAi, mewRNAi and ifRNAi.
source: We tested for their role in the ASP by expressing RNAi constructs, and observed that whereas the ASP developed normally in the presence of scbRNAi, αPS4RNAi, αPS5RNAi and βvRNAi (Figure 8—figure supplement 1A–D), ASP development was abnormal in the presence of mysRNAi, mewRNAi and ifRNAi (Figure 8A–D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by images in Figure 8A-D.

claim: The ASP developed normally in the presence of scbRNAi, αPS4RNAi, αPS5RNAi and βvRNAi.
source: We tested for their role in the ASP by expressing RNAi constructs, and observed that whereas the ASP developed normally in the presence of scbRNAi, αPS4RNAi, αPS5RNAi and βvRNAi (Figure 8—figure supplement 1A–D), ASP development was abnormal in the presence of mysRNAi, mewRNAi and ifRNAi (Figure 8A–D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by images in Figure 8—figure supplement 1A-D.

claim: FGF and Dpp signaling in the ASP were reduced in the presence of mysRNAi, mewRNAi, or ifRNAi.
source: FGF and Dpp signaling in the ASP were reduced in the presence of mysRNAi, mewRNAi, or ifRNAi (Figure 8E–L); and relative numbers of cytonemes were also reduced (Figure 8M).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by images in Figure 8E-L and quantification in Figure 8M.

claim: Relative numbers of cytonemes were reduced in the presence of mysRNAi, mewRNAi, or ifRNAi.
source: FGF and Dpp signaling in the ASP were reduced in the presence of mysRNAi, mewRNAi, or ifRNAi (Figure 8E–L); and relative numbers of cytonemes were also reduced (Figure 8M).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by quantification in Figure 8M.

claim: Expression of mysRNAi and mewRNAi had no apparent effect on the number of dividing or apoptotic cells.
source: Expression of mysRNAi and mewRNAi had no apparent effect on the number of dividing or apoptotic cells, on cell shape or on the ability of ASP cells to activate Dpp signal transduction (Figure 8—figure supplement 1E–N).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by images in Figure 8—figure supplement 1E-N.

claim: Expression of mysRNAi and mewRNAi had no apparent effect on cell shape.
source: Expression of mysRNAi and mewRNAi had no apparent effect on the number of dividing or apoptotic cells, on cell shape or on the ability of ASP cells to activate Dpp signal transduction (Figure 8—figure supplement 1E–N).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by images in Figure 8—figure supplement 1E-N.

claim: Expression of mysRNAi and mewRNAi had no apparent effect on the ability of ASP cells to activate Dpp signal transduction.
source: Expression of mysRNAi and mewRNAi had no apparent effect on the number of dividing or apoptotic cells, on cell shape or on the ability of ASP cells to activate Dpp signal transduction (Figure 8—figure supplement 1E–N).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by images in Figure 8—figure supplement 1K-N.

claim: GFP fluorescence was visible at the juxtaposition of the ASP and wing disc in controls using the GRASP technique.
source: As shown in Figure 8 (panels N-Q), GFP fluorescence was visible at the juxtaposition of the ASP and wing disc in controls, but fluorescence was markedly reduced in preparations from animals that expressed mysRNAi.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by images in Figure 8N,P.

claim: GFP fluorescence was markedly reduced in preparations from animals that expressed mysRNAi using the GRASP technique.
source: As shown in Figure 8 (panels N-Q), GFP fluorescence was visible at the juxtaposition of the ASP and wing disc in controls, but fluorescence was markedly reduced in preparations from animals that expressed mysRNAi.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by images in Figure 8O,Q.

claim: Integrin function is required by ASP cytonemes and for signaling in the ASP.
source: We conclude that integrin function is required by ASP cytonemes and for signaling in the ASP.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a conclusion based on the integrin RNAi data.

claim: Ilk:GFP localizes in puncta along and at the tips of ASP cytonemes.
source: We expressed an Ilk:GFP fusion construct in the ASP and observed GFP fluorescence in puncta along and at the tips of ASP cytonemes (Figure 8R).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by images in Figure 8R.

claim: Expression of IlkRNAi in the ASP perturbed ASP morphogenesis and reduced the number of ASP cytonemes.
source: Expression of IlkRNAi in the ASP perturbed ASP morphogenesis and reduced the number of ASP cytonemes (Figure 8S).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by images in Figure 8S.

claim: Laminin is present in the ECM of the wing disc.
source: Laminin is an integrin ligand that has been implicated in many developmental and disease contexts, and it is present in the ECM of the wing disc (Figure 7E,F) where it is dependent on pk function (Figure 5H,I).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by images in Figure 7E,F.

claim: Laminin in the wing disc ECM is dependent on pk function.
source: Laminin is an integrin ligand that has been implicated in many developmental and disease contexts, and it is present in the ECM of the wing disc (Figure 7E,F) where it is dependent on pk function (Figure 5H,I).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by images in Figure 5H,I.

claim: wb encodes the α subunit of laminin.
source: To determine if wing disc laminin is necessary for the ASP, we depleted laminin in the disc by expressing an RNAi construct that targets the α subunit of laminin that is encoded by the wing blister (wb) gene.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as background information.

claim: wb has been shown to interact genetically with mys.
source: wb has been shown to interact genetically with mys (Martin et al., 1999; Schöck and Perrimon, 2003), which encodes a β integrin subunit; the Wb laminin, which has an RGD domain, has been shown to interact with both αPS1 and αPS2 integrins (Gotwals et al., 1994; Graner et al., 1998).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by citations to previous work.

claim: mys encodes a β integrin subunit.
source: wb has been shown to interact genetically with mys (Martin et al., 1999; Schöck and Perrimon, 2003), which encodes a β integrin subunit; the Wb laminin, which has an RGD domain, has been shown to interact with both αPS1 and αPS2 integrins (Gotwals et al., 1994; Graner et al., 1998).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as established knowledge.

claim: The Wb laminin has an RGD domain.
source: wb has been shown to interact genetically with mys (Martin et al., 1999; Schöck and Perrimon, 2003), which encodes a β integrin subunit; the Wb laminin, which has an RGD domain, has been shown to interact with both αPS1 and αPS2 integrins (Gotwals et al., 1994; Graner et al., 1998).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by citations to previous work.

claim: The Wb laminin has been shown to interact with both αPS1 and αPS2 integrins.
source: wb has been shown to interact genetically with mys (Martin et al., 1999; Schöck and Perrimon, 2003), which encodes a β integrin subunit; the Wb laminin, which has an RGD domain, has been shown to interact with both αPS1 and αPS2 integrins (Gotwals et al., 1994; Graner et al., 1998).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by citations to previous work.

claim: The wb knockdown genotype had a shortened and malformed ASP with reduced numbers of cytonemes.
source: The wb knockdown genotype had a shortened and malformed ASP with reduced numbers of cytonemes (Figures 8M, 9A), and low levels of Dpp (Figure 9E) and FGF signaling (Figure 9I).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by images in Figures 8M and 9A.

claim: The wb knockdown genotype had low levels of Dpp and FGF signaling.
source: The wb knockdown genotype had a shortened and malformed ASP with reduced numbers of cytonemes (Figures 8M, 9A), and low levels of Dpp (Figure 9E) and FGF signaling (Figure 9I).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by images in Figure 9E,I.

claim: wb/+ and mew/+ heterozygotes survived and developed normal ASPs that had normal levels of Dpp and FGF signaling.
source: Mutants that lack functional wb or mew are inviable, but wb/+ and mew/+ heterozygotes survived and developed normal ASPs that had normal levels of Dpp and FGF signaling (Figure 9B,C,F,G,J,K).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by images in Figure 9B,C,F,G,J,K.

claim: Mutants that lack functional wb or mew are inviable.
source: Mutants that lack functional wb or mew are inviable, but wb/+ and mew/+ heterozygotes survived and developed normal ASPs that had normal levels of Dpp and FGF signaling (Figure 9B,C,F,G,J,K).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as established knowledge.

claim: mew/+; wb/+ double heterozygotes produced abnormal ASPs that had reduced numbers of cytonemes and reduced Dpp and FGF signaling.
source: In contrast, mew/+; wb/+ double heterozygotes produced abnormal ASPs that had reduced numbers of cytonemes and reduced Dpp and FGF signaling (Figure 9D,H,L and Table 2).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by images in Figure 9D,H,L and data in Table 2.

claim: The Wb laminin is a ligand for integrin-dependent cytoneme-ECM interactions.
source: These results suggest that the Wb laminin is a ligand for integrin-dependent cytoneme-ECM interactions.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an interpretation of the genetic interaction data.

claim: The extracellular environment in which cytonemes navigate is organized and structured and provides essential support that is specific to different cytoneme types.
source: The results show that the extracellular environment in which cytonemes navigate is organized and structured and provides essential support that is specific to different cytoneme types.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a summary of the findings.

claim: Cytonemes are dynamic, and their orientations change during development.
source: Cytonemes are dynamic, and their orientations change during development as the tissues that make them grow and the spatial relationship between the cells that produce signaling proteins and the responding cells changes (Bischoff et al., 2013; Roy et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Cytonemes change in response to ectopic over-expression of signaling proteins.
source: They also change in response to ectopic over-expression of signaling proteins (Guha et al., 2009; Roy et al., 2011; Sato and Kornberg, 2002).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by citations to previous work.

claim: The strong mutant phenotypes in the ASP had not been noted in previous studies of PCP mutants.
source: The strong mutant phenotypes in the ASP had not been noted in previous studies of PCP mutants, the most likely reason being that the dorsal air sacs are not visible in intact flies and flies that lack dorsal air sacs are viable (Guha et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as an explanation for why these phenotypes were not previously reported.

claim: Flies that lack dorsal air sacs are viable.
source: The strong mutant phenotypes in the ASP had not been noted in previous studies of PCP mutants, the most likely reason being that the dorsal air sacs are not visible in intact flies and flies that lack dorsal air sacs are viable (Guha et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Specific requirements of Dally for Dpp signaling have been reported previously.
source: Specific requirements of Dally for Dpp signaling (Dejima et al., 2011) and of Dlp for FGF signaling (Yan and Lin 2007) have been reported previously and have been interpreted as evidence that Dally and Dlp function as co-receptors; modifications of the Dally and Dlp heparan sulfate backbones have been proposed as structures that provide specificity for the respective signaling systems (Kamimura et al., 2006 and reviewed in Nakato and Kimata, 2002).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Specific requirements of Dlp for FGF signaling have been reported previously.
source: Specific requirements of Dally for Dpp signaling (Dejima et al., 2011) and of Dlp for FGF signaling (Yan and Lin 2007) have been reported previously and have been interpreted as evidence that Dally and Dlp function as co-receptors; modifications of the Dally and Dlp heparan sulfate backbones have been proposed as structures that provide specificity for the respective signaling systems (Kamimura et al., 2006 and reviewed in Nakato and Kimata, 2002).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Dally and Dlp have been interpreted as functioning as co-receptors.
source: Specific requirements of Dally for Dpp signaling (Dejima et al., 2011) and of Dlp for FGF signaling (Yan and Lin 2007) have been reported previously and have been interpreted as evidence that Dally and Dlp function as co-receptors; modifications of the Dally and Dlp heparan sulfate backbones have been proposed as structures that provide specificity for the respective signaling systems (Kamimura et al., 2006 and reviewed in Nakato and Kimata, 2002).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Modifications of the Dally and Dlp heparan sulfate backbones have been proposed as structures that provide specificity for the respective signaling systems.
source: Specific requirements of Dally for Dpp signaling (Dejima et al., 2011) and of Dlp for FGF signaling (Yan and Lin 2007) have been reported previously and have been interpreted as evidence that Dally and Dlp function as co-receptors; modifications of the Dally and Dlp heparan sulfate backbones have been proposed as structures that provide specificity for the respective signaling systems (Kamimura et al., 2006 and reviewed in Nakato and Kimata, 2002).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Each HSPG provides a substrate that supports cytoneme extension and/or stability.
source: Our observation that Tkv- and Btl-containing cytoneme subtypes were not present in areas that lacked Dally or Dlp, respectively (Figure 6), suggests that each HSPG provides a substrate that supports cytoneme extension and/or stability.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as an interpretation of the clonal analysis data.

claim: Cytonemes interact directly and specifically with the HSPGs.
source: This implies that cytonemes interact directly and specifically with the HSPGs and that the roles of these ECM components are not limited to co-receptor functions.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as an interpretation of the findings.

claim: The roles of Dally and Dlp are not limited to co-receptor functions.
source: This implies that cytonemes interact directly and specifically with the HSPGs and that the roles of these ECM components are not limited to co-receptor functions.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as an interpretation of the findings.

claim: Signaling proteins that have been observed between signal producing and receiving cells are cytoneme-associated and are neither extracellular nor ECM-bound.
source: Our discovery that cytonemes traffic signaling proteins between cells (Roy et al., 2014) revealed that signaling proteins that have been observed between signal producing and receiving cells are cytoneme-associated and are neither extracellular nor ECM-bound (Roy and Kornberg, 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by citations to previous work.

claim: The cytonemes that mediate Dpp and FGF signaling contact the ECM directly in ways that involve both integrins and specific HSPG interactions.
source: Our findings are consistent with the idea that secreted signaling proteins and signaling protein receptors are not distributed in the extracellular environment and are not bound to the ECM, but rather that the cytonemes that mediate Dpp and FGF signaling contact the ECM directly in ways that involve both integrins and specific HSPG interactions.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as an interpretation of the findings.
